statement: Reconstruct four haplotypes from a pooled tetraploid long-read experiment. The frozen benchmark combines real PacBio reads from human samples HG00514 and NA19240, as used by the official WhatsHap polyphase test and publication. Forty-two biallelic sites have known allele dosages, while noisy and incomplete reads ambiguously originate from one of four unordered haplotypes.
constraints: Return four complete binary haplotypes across exactly V001 through V042.
At every variant, the sum of alternate alleles across the four haplotypes must equal the frozen genotype dosage.
The four haplotype labels are exchangeable and are scored permutation-invariantly within each supported phase block.
Infer defensible phase-block boundaries rather than asserting unsupported continuity across evidence gaps.
Every alternative-domain worker must solve the complete four-haplotype problem, not one haplotype, block, or site subset.
Use only frozen public evidence and representation-neutral Broker computations. Held-out phased output is unavailable until scoring.
question: What are the four dosage-consistent haplotypes and defensible phase blocks across all 42 sites?

evidence_catalog.access: Representation-neutral latent.* tools expose sealed full-problem projections.

provenance.data_kind: real PacBio alignments pooled into an artificial tetraploid benchmark

required_outputs: Four complete haplotypes over V001 through V042
Exact satisfaction of every public allele dosage
A public objective and robustness certificate
